label: Fresh funding
description: The company recently raised capital and is likely to have a growth mandate.
play: Connect the new growth mandate to a repeatable hook-testing system.

label: New marketing leader
description: A new marketing decision-maker is entering a high-change window.
play: Offer a fast baseline of current creative, audience response and immediate wins.

label: Product launch
description: A product, service or major feature is entering the market.
play: Build and test the launch narrative across paid and organic creative.

label: Market expansion
description: The company is entering a new geography, segment or distribution channel.
play: Translate the brand into locally relevant hooks for the new audience.

label: Major partnership
description: A partnership creates a new story and distribution moment.
play: Turn the partnership announcement into audience-specific creative angles.

label: Contract or grant awarded
description: A meaningful contract creates budget, legitimacy and a communications need.
play: Use the award as proof while translating it into buyer-facing hooks.

label: Marketing hiring surge
description: Multiple marketing hires indicate active investment and an execution gap.
play: Help the growing team establish hooks and test infrastructure while it staffs up.

label: Agency or partner search
description: The company is explicitly evaluating an agency, consultant or creative partner.
play: Respond directly to the stated brief with an evidence-backed opportunity map.

label: Advertising started
description: The company has begun running paid media.
play: Review whether the new campaign has enough message and creative variation.

label: Advertising volume spike
description: Paid campaign volume increased materially, indicating budget and urgency.
play: Match the spend increase with a larger, measured hook portfolio.

label: Creative refresh hypothesis
description: Creative age, repetition or exposure warrants review; these proxies do not establish fatigue or poor performance.
play: Review the observed creative patterns alongside performance data before proposing a refresh; successful long-running ads may still be effective.

label: Low hook diversity
description: Most active ads rely on the same concept, opening or claim.
play: Quantify concept concentration and introduce a structured testing matrix.

label: Social engagement declining
description: Content output is no longer earning proportional audience response.
play: Identify the exhausted message pattern and mine new hooks from audience language.

label: Breakout content
description: A piece of content is performing far above the brand baseline.
play: Extract the winning premise and scale it before the attention window closes.

label: Search demand spike
description: Brand or category search demand is rising quickly.
play: Align paid and organic messaging with the emerging search intent.

label: Traffic spike
description: The company is receiving an unusual increase in attention.
play: Help convert the temporary attention into durable customer demand.

label: Conversion gap
description: Attention or spend is growing while conversion performance is weak.
play: Trace the promise from ad opening through landing page and rebuild message continuity.

label: Rebrand or major website change
description: The company changed its identity, positioning or central message.
play: Test whether the new positioning translates into compelling audience-first hooks.

label: Pricing or packaging changed
description: A commercial change requires clear value communication.
play: Translate the new package and price into concrete, audience-specific value.

label: Marketing technology upgrade
description: New advertising, analytics or lifecycle technology indicates investment readiness.
play: Connect the new stack to a disciplined hook experimentation program.

label: Customer sentiment declining
description: Ratings or review sentiment have deteriorated.
play: Separate delivery problems from message problems and use authentic customer language carefully.

label: Review velocity spike
description: Customer activity or attention has increased materially.
play: Turn the current customer language and proof into credible creative angles.

label: Competitor campaign pressure
description: A competitor is increasing advertising or winning audience attention.
play: Find a differentiated attention territory instead of copying the competitor's message.

label: Upcoming event or seasonal window
description: An approaching event creates a finite audience-attention window.
play: Prepare event-specific hooks and activate before demand peaks.

label: High first-party intent
description: A known account is showing direct buying or evaluation behavior.
play: Route immediately to an owner with the specific behavior and relevant proof.

label: Existing relationship
description: The account has a prior customer, partner, referral or conversation relationship.
play: Use the known relationship and new trigger rather than sending cold outreach.

label: New physical location
description: A physical opening creates a local awareness and conversion deadline.
play: Build local creative around the opening window, neighborhood and customer occasion.

label: Acquisition or merger
description: A corporate combination creates positioning, audience and integration work.
play: Clarify what changed, why it matters and how each audience should understand it.

label: Marketing efficiency pressure
description: The company is under pressure to improve marketing efficiency.
play: Position hook quality as the fastest controllable lever before cutting distribution.

label: Active crisis
description: An active safety, legal or reputational crisis makes automated sales outreach inappropriate.
play: Suppress automated contact and require human review.

label: Major layoffs
description: Material layoffs may reduce buying capacity or make outreach insensitive.
play: Delay generic outreach; verify budget and context before contact.
